quiz_item.question: If an athlete receives a blow to the head or body during practice or competition and shows signs of dizziness, confusion, headache, or balance problems, what action must be taken immediately?
options: A. Have the athlete drink cold water on the sideline for five minutes and return to the game if the score is close.
B. Remove the athlete from play immediately to prevent second-impact syndrome, notify parents and coaches, and do not allow a return to play until cleared by a licensed healthcare professional.
C. Have the athlete perform vigorous sprint intervals to test whether their vision clears up.
D. Give the athlete aspirin on the bench and let them finish the current half before evaluating symptoms.

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Remove the athlete from play immediately to prevent second-impact syndrome, notify parents and coaches, and do not allow a return to play until cleared by a licensed healthcare professional.

B. It lowers body temperature in the extremities while increasing bone density.
C. It causes excess water retention in the leg muscles during aerobic exercise.
D. It blocks digestive enzymes from absorbing dietary carbohydrates.
choices: A. It coats the lungs with sticky tars and injures the airways and air sacs needed for peak lung capacity.
B. It lowers body temperature in the extremities while increasing bone density.
C. It causes excess water retention in the leg muscles during aerobic exercise.
D. It blocks digestive enzymes from absorbing dietary carbohydrates.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. It coats the lungs with sticky tars and injures the airways and air sacs needed for peak lung capacity.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Tobacco smoke interferes with lung growth, coats the lungs with sticky tars, and damages airways and air sacs, leaving athletes gasping for air (p. 10).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why does the Sports merit badge pamphlet emphasize writing down your personal training plan and development goals?
quiz_item.question: Why does the Sports merit badge pamphlet emphasize writing down your personal training plan and development goals?
options: A. Written logs allow you to skip pre-season physical exams and warm-ups.
B. Coaches only allow athletes with identical training schedules to compete in games.
C. A written plan guides how you will reach your goals and lets you look back on your progress to set new targets.
D. Written charts replace the requirement to participate in an organized season.
choices: A. Written logs allow you to skip pre-season physical exams and warm-ups.
B. Coaches only allow athletes with identical training schedules to compete in games.
C. A written plan guides how you will reach your goals and lets you look back on your progress to set new targets.
D. Written charts replace the requirement to participate in an organized season.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. A written plan guides how you will reach your goals and lets you look back on your progress to set new targets.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Writing down your training and development plan provides clear direction, rewards you with a record of how far you have progressed, and helps you set new goals (p. 25).

requirements.description: Do ONE of the following: (a) Identify three career opportunities that would use skills and knowledge related to a sport. Pick one and research the training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (b) Identify how you might use skills and knowledge related to a sport to pursue a personal hobby and/or healthy lifestyle. Research the additional training required, expenses, and affiliation with organizations that would help you maximize the enjoyment and benefit you might gain from it. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and share what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: If an athlete receives a blow to the head or body during practice or competition and shows signs of dizziness, confusion, headache, or balance problems, what action must be taken immediately?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: If an athlete receives a blow to the head or body during practice or competition and shows signs of dizziness, confusion, headache, or balance problems, what action must be taken immediately?
options: A. Have the athlete drink cold water on the sideline for five minutes and return to the game if the score is close.
B. Remove the athlete from play immediately to prevent second-impact syndrome, notify parents and coaches, and do not allow a return to play until cleared by a licensed healthcare professional.
C. Have the athlete perform vigorous sprint intervals to test whether their vision clears up.
D. Give the athlete aspirin on the bench and let them finish the current half before evaluating symptoms.
choices: A. Have the athlete drink cold water on the sideline for five minutes and return to the game if the score is close.
B. Remove the athlete from play immediately to prevent second-impact syndrome, notify parents and coaches, and do not allow a return to play until cleared by a licensed healthcare professional.
C. Have the athlete perform vigorous sprint intervals to test whether their vision clears up.
D. Give the athlete aspirin on the bench and let them finish the current half before evaluating symptoms.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Remove the athlete from play immediately to prevent second-impact syndrome, notify parents and coaches, and do not allow a return to play until cleared by a licensed healthcare professional.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Any suspected concussion requires immediate removal from play ('when in doubt, sit them out') and formal medical clearance before returning, as a second head impact before recovery can be catastrophic.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does tobacco smoke directly reduce an athlete's stamina and respiratory performance?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does tobacco smoke directly reduce an athlete's stamina and respiratory performance?
options: A. It coats the lungs with sticky tars and injures the airways and air sacs needed for peak lung capacity.
B. It lowers body temperature in the extremities while increasing bone density.
C. It causes excess water retention in the leg muscles during aerobic exercise.
D. It blocks digestive enzymes from absorbing dietary carbohydrates.
choices: A. It coats the lungs with sticky tars and injures the airways and air sacs needed for peak lung capacity.
B. It lowers body temperature in the extremities while increasing bone density.
C. It causes excess water retention in the leg muscles during aerobic exercise.
D. It blocks digestive enzymes from absorbing dietary carbohydrates.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It coats the lungs with sticky tars and injures the airways and air sacs needed for peak lung capacity.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Tobacco smoke interferes with lung growth, coats the lungs with sticky tars, and damages airways and air sacs, leaving athletes gasping for air (p. 10).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the Sports merit badge pamphlet, how should a Scout respond when they disagree with a ruling made by a game official or referee?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the Sports merit badge pamphlet, how should a Scout respond when they disagree with a ruling made by a game official or referee?
options: A. Refuse to resume play until the referee reviews the call with both coaches.
B. Encourage spectators in the stands to boo the official so the next call goes your way.
C. Put yourself in the official's shoes, accept the decision, and show Scout spirit.
D. Retaliate against the opposing player on the next play to even the score.
choices: A. Refuse to resume play until the referee reviews the call with both coaches.
B. Encourage spectators in the stands to boo the official so the next call goes your way.
C. Put yourself in the official's shoes, accept the decision, and show Scout spirit.
D. Retaliate against the opposing player on the next play to even the score.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Put yourself in the official's shoes, accept the decision, and show Scout spirit.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Good sportsmanship means putting yourself in the official's shoes, recognizing that the call was fair from their viewpoint, and displaying cheerful Scout spirit (p. 22).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the proper etiquette for players and spectators when an injured athlete on the field recovers or is carried off?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the proper etiquette for players and spectators when an injured athlete on the field recovers or is carried off?
options: A. Turn away from the field and chant for the backup player to enter the game.
B. Boo the opposing team for causing a delay in the game clock.
C. Question the referee about whether the injury timeout was legitimate.
D. Clap politely in appreciation of the injured player's effort.
choices: A. Turn away from the field and chant for the backup player to enter the game.
B. Boo the opposing team for causing a delay in the game clock.
C. Question the referee about whether the injury timeout was legitimate.
D. Clap politely in appreciation of the injured player's effort.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Clap politely in appreciation of the injured player's effort.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Good sports etiquette calls for spectators and players to clap respectfully for their team, never boo opponents, and clap in appreciation when an injured player recovers or leaves the field (p. 27).
